name: genocide
definition: Under the Genocide Convention, genocide involves specified acts committed with the intent to destroy all or part of a national, ethnic, racial or religious group because it is that group. The acts include killing members, seriously harming them, and forcibly transferring children of the group to another group.

name: primary source
definition: Original evidence directly connected to the historical question, such as an object, record or first-hand account. A memoir or oral history recorded later can also be a primary source. Its date, purpose, memory and mediation still need examination.

name: patronage
definition: Support or commissioning of work by a person or institution, shaping what makers could produce.

name: tomb
definition: A place prepared for the dead. Its objects may reflect the beliefs and resources of those arranging the burial.

name: estate
definition: A substantial property and the land, buildings and labor that sustain it.

name: afterlife
definition: Beliefs about an existence after death. Historians study how people represented and practiced these beliefs.

name: evidence
definition: Information used to support or challenge an account of the past. Objects, written records and spoken testimony can all provide evidence. Each needs to be understood in context.

name: inference
definition: An explanation drawn from evidence rather than something directly observed.

name: chronology
definition: The ordering and dating of events. Dates can be approximate, disputed or revised.

name: ritual
definition: An action or sequence given particular shared significance, often repeated in a religious or social setting.

name: dynasty
definition: A sequence of rulers associated with one family; it is not the same thing as a whole society.

name: empire
definition: A political formation ruling over diverse territories and peoples, often through conquest and unequal power.

name: freedman
definition: A formerly enslaved man. The label identifies a past legal status, not the full experience of a person.

name: caravan
definition: People and pack animals traveling together, often carrying goods.

name: inscription
definition: Words deliberately written or cut on a surface. The author’s purposes and audience matter.

name: coinage
definition: Coins and the practices through which authorities issue and people use them.

name: provenance
definition: The documented history of an object, including its origins, past ownership and previous locations. Archaeologists distinguish this from provenience: the recorded location where an object was found. A find context also includes surroundings and associations. Knowing one part of this history does not fill gaps in another.

name: port
definition: A place where vessels land and goods or people enter a wider network.

name: stele
definition: An upright stone monument, often carved or inscribed.

name: archaeology
definition: Study of the past through material remains and their contexts.

name: irrigation
definition: Directing water to fields. The channels and their maintenance involve both environments and people.

name: tribute
definition: Goods or labor demanded by a political authority. Its precise form varies by setting.

name: iconography
definition: The study of imagery and its meanings in a particular context.

name: regalia
definition: Objects that represent office, rank or authority.

name: material culture
definition: Things people make and use, studied as part of social life.

name: enslavement
definition: The coercive treatment of people as property, denying freedom and exploiting their work.

name: colonialism
definition: Control of people and territories by an outside power, involving unequal political and economic relationships.

name: decolonization
definition: Processes of ending colonial rule; political independence did not automatically end every inequality.

name: archive
definition: A collection of records, shaped by decisions about what was created, kept, lost and made accessible.

name: industrialization
definition: Changes in production involving machines, energy, workplaces and labor organization; timing and effects differ by region.

name: earthwork
definition: A deliberately shaped construction of earth, such as a mound or enclosure. Its form alone does not establish its purpose or governing system.

name: terminus post quem
definition: The earliest possible date for an event, given the evidence. A timber could only have been used in a wall in or after the year its last surviving ring grew. The wood may have been stored or reused.

name: calibration
definition: Converting a radiocarbon determination into possible calendar dates using an independently established reference curve. One determination can have more than one plausible calendar placement.

name: syllabary
definition: A writing system whose signs represent syllables. The Cherokee syllabary is a system for writing Cherokee, not an ornamental version of English.

name: wampum
definition: Worked shell beads used in particular Indigenous contexts. The Onondaga account here explains agreements, speakers, memory and responsibilities; a pattern does not interpret itself.

name: ratification
definition: A formal act of confirming an agreement through a government’s procedures. It can occur after negotiation and signing, and does not by itself prove that commitments were fulfilled.

name: manoomin
definition: The Ojibwe name for wild rice, explained in the community sources as food with physical, cultural and spiritual significance. Related practices differ among communities.

name: winnowing
definition: Separating grain from lighter chaff, often with the help of moving air. It is one stage of finishing rice, distinct from harvesting, drying, parching and hulling.

name: marine reservoir effect
definition: Marine carbon can give a sample a different radiocarbon age from a contemporary land-based sample. Appropriate calibration and reservoir corrections matter; a regional revision does not automatically redetermine every catalogued object.

name: reconstruction
definition: A modern interpretation made from evidence about an earlier object, building or practice. It can help investigate how something worked, while remaining distinct from the surviving original.

name: radiocarbon
definition: A method that estimates the age of once-living material from radioactive carbon. Samples, calibration and environmental effects matter; an uncalibrated age in years BP is not automatically a calendar year.

name: waterlogged preservation
definition: Survival of material in persistently wet conditions that slow some forms of decay. The preserved material is still a selective record, not a complete picture of a household.

name: seasonal round
definition: An organized pattern of activities and movement through the year. Mobility can depend on detailed knowledge, planning and social institutions.

name: cache pit
definition: A prepared underground storage space. Its construction, contents and use require evidence; an explanatory model is not an excavated original.

name: repatriation
definition: Return of belongings or ancestral remains to the peoples or communities to whom they belong. The atlas follows the particular community account rather than assuming one process for every collection.

name: potlatch
definition: A ceremony with specific forms and responsibilities in different Northwest Coast communities. In the Kwakwaka’wakw account here, invited people witness consequential events and gifts acknowledge their role.

name: experimental archaeology
definition: Testing an interpretation by reproducing a material, technique or activity under stated conditions. An experiment supports a possibility; it is not a recovered ancient event.

name: archaeological tradition
definition: A research label for related material practices across places or times. It is not automatically the name of one people, language or state.

name: biomarker
definition: A detectable chemical or biological trace used as evidence of a substance or process. Its interpretation depends on the method, sample and alternative explanations.

name: kiva
definition: A Pueblo ceremonial space with varied forms and histories. Archaeological identification and living community knowledge both matter; not every circular room has an identical meaning.

name: proxy
definition: An indirect measurement used to investigate something not directly counted or observed. A lake-sediment signal, for example, requires interpretation before it becomes a population claim.

name: chiefdom
definition: An analytical term for a society with ranked authority and leadership above a local community. Its use for an archaeological case is an interpretation, not a surviving official name.

name: stonepaste
definition: A ceramic body containing abundant crushed quartz with clay and glassy material. It differs from porcelain even when makers adapt similar designs.

name: tughra
definition: A calligraphic emblem of an Ottoman sultan’s authority used on official documents and other media. Drawing and ornament could involve specialized makers.

name: forced relocation
definition: Movement imposed on people by authorities or armed power. Later achievements or privileges do not make the original movement voluntary.

name: caravansary
definition: An establishment offering space and facilities for traveling merchants and their goods, often linked to urban markets or overland travel.

name: madrasa
definition: An institution of learning in Islamic societies, with varied subjects, forms and patronage across time and place. A building does not by itself reveal every student’s experience.

name: lacquer
definition: A protective, often glossy surface finish applied over painted or decorated material. The Iranian case here uses painted papier-mâché and pasteboard.

name: sovereignty
definition: A claim to supreme political authority, including independence from another state. A declaration, recognition by other states and effective control can have different dates and histories.

name: federation
definition: A political arrangement in which powers are divided between a central government and constituent governments. Its actual distribution of authority must be read in the particular constitution or agreement.

name: Standardization
definition: An attempt to establish common units, forms or procedures. An announced standard and the way people use it are separate historical questions.

name: Dhamma
definition: In Ashoka’s messages, a moral and administrative program concerning conduct and government. Its uses need context and are not identical with a complete statement of Buddhist doctrine.

name: Deme
definition: A local civic community in ancient Attica. The late-fourth-century Athenian account describes scrutiny and enrollment of eligible young men among its members.

name: Stratigraphy
definition: The sequence and relationships of archaeological layers and features. An object’s manufacture date and the date or history of the deposit containing it are different questions.

name: Endowment
definition: A grant of land, property or resources intended to support an institution over time. Its terms and the work supplying that support need their own evidence.

name: Mit’a
definition: Rotating labor service required by Inca authorities. It differs from permanent or semi-permanent resettlement; provisioning does not by itself establish equal choice or returns.

name: Jeli / jeliw
definition: A Mande specialist in oral traditions and performance, with roles including genealogy, praise and diplomacy. Jeliw is plural; particular performances have their own dates, audiences and purposes.

name: Provisioning
definition: Organizing and supplying the food and other materials needed by people or institutions. Storage, preparation and delivery involve different tasks.

name: Shicra
definition: A woven plant-fiber bag. Stone-filled examples occur in Caral’s construction deposits; their presence alone does not establish how every worker was recruited or required to contribute.

name: Midden
definition: An accumulation of discarded material and occupation deposits. Its contents and layers can help investigate activities, but need their own context and chronology.

name: Temper
definition: Non-clay material, such as sand or plant fibers, mixed with clay to change how pottery behaves. Its composition can help investigate material sources, without identifying a particular carrier or voyage.

name: Type-site
definition: A place whose name supplies the label for an archaeological category. Similar finds elsewhere still need their own dates and contexts; the name alone does not prove that practices spread outward from that place.

name: LiDAR
definition: Light detection and ranging: measurements of light pulses used to model elevation. A ground-surface model can reveal forms, while excavation and dating help investigate their histories.

name: Faience
definition: A manufactured, usually quartz-rich material with a glazed surface. Ancient Egyptian and Kushite faience is distinct from a granite carving or ordinary clay pottery; a mould and production debris can help investigate its making.

name: Shabti
definition: A funerary figure intended to substitute for work required of the deceased in the afterlife. Its name, material, inscription and find context need their own evidence; a royal example does not represent every household’s beliefs.

name: Plain weave
definition: A way of making cloth. The crosswise thread (weft) passes over one lengthwise thread (warp) and under the next. On the return row, the pattern reverses. A diagram shows the method. Identifying the weave of a particular cloth requires examining its threads.

name: Residential compound
definition: A connected group of rooms and open spaces used for living and other activities. An archaeological compound may include production, storage and gathering; its walls do not by themselves identify one nuclear family or its legal status.

name: Find context
definition: The recorded place and associations in which something was found, including its position, surrounding material and relationship to other features. A regional style or present museum location does not supply a precise archaeological find context.

name: Relief
definition: An image carved or modelled so that forms project from a background surface. A relief can organize a story on that surface; its interpretation and use require further evidence.

name: Iconoclasm
definition: Opposition to or destruction of images, especially in religious settings. Byzantine disputes involved particular periods and policies; the term does not describe every Christian view about images.

name: Masonry
definition: Building with stone, brick or similar units. Facing stones and a rubble core can perform different tasks within one wall; its materials alone do not identify every builder or the institution organizing the work.

name: Workshop
definition: A setting or group in which people produce or prepare work. Size, training, ownership and the division of tasks vary; a catalogue’s workshop attribution does not identify every maker.
